ISTJ.want: The satisfaction of seeing things through, and the security of being trusted
ISTJ.effort: Following rules and steps, and building up without mistakes
ISTJ.work: Work with clear rules and steps, where accuracy is valued

ISFJ.want: Feeling useful to others, and a place where you feel safe
ISFJ.effort: Thinking ahead, paying attention, and supporting those around you
ISFJ.work: Work where you support people close to you and get thanked directly

INFJ.want: A sense of being part of something meaningful, and relationships where you truly understand each other
INFJ.effort: Reading people's feelings and picking up on what goes unsaid
INFJ.work: Work where you can be part of people's growth and inner lives for the long run

INTJ.want: The satisfaction of moving things with a plan you made, and time alone to think deeply
INTJ.effort: Looking ahead, laying out the logic, and showing the shortest route
INTJ.work: Work where you're trusted with long-term strategy and building systems

ISTP.want: The freedom to solve problems with your own hands and head, and time without interference
ISTP.effort: Fixing problems calmly and quickly when they come up
ISTP.work: Work where the results of your hands-on effort are plain to see

ISFP.want: Being honest about what you love, and calm relationships
ISFP.effort: Keeping the peace and softening the mood with your own sense of things
ISFP.work: Work where you can use your sensitivity and go at your own pace

INFP.want: Being able to honor your values, and a purpose you truly care about
INFP.effort: Staying close to people's feelings and putting ideals into words or form
INFP.work: Work where you can express what you believe in

INTP.want: The freedom to think things through as deeply as you like, and intellectual stimulation
INTP.effort: Analyzing how things work, then finding and fixing contradictions
INTP.work: A place where thinking itself is the job

ESTP.want: The thrill of moving and seeing results right away, and competing in the moment
ESTP.effort: Acting without hesitation and grabbing the chance in front of you
ESTP.work: Work where speed and action turn straight into results

ESFP.want: Sharing fun with people, and savoring the moment
ESFP.effort: Brightening the room and making everyone have a good time
ESFP.work: Work where you deal with people directly and see them smile

ENFP.want: Exciting possibilities, and the joy of connecting with people
ENFP.effort: Coming up with ideas and getting people on board to start something new
ENFP.work: Work full of new projects and new people

ENTP.want: The freedom to try new ideas, and smart debates
ENTP.effort: Questioning the usual and finding a breakthrough from another angle
ENTP.work: Work with lots of change, where ideas win

ESTJ.want: The satisfaction of organizing things and moving them forward, and a role with responsibility
ESTJ.effort: Setting up the plan, bringing people together, and getting results
ESTJ.work: Work where you run an organization and see results in numbers

ESFJ.want: A place where everyone gets along, and the joy of being thanked
ESFJ.effort: Connecting people and keeping things in harmony
ESFJ.work: Work where you engage with your team or community and can be the one who pulls it together

ENFJ.want: Bringing out people's potential, and relationships built on trust
ENFJ.effort: Encouraging people and uniting the team toward a goal
ENFJ.work: Work where you grow and guide people

ENTJ.want: Moving people and things toward a big goal, and the freedom to make the call
ENTJ.effort: Making decisions, moving people efficiently, and getting results
ENTJ.work: Work where you have decision-making power and can aim for big results

worry: Time with people is fun, but you're drained on the way home
You can't say no to invitations and your schedule fills up
People see you as cheerful, so no one notices when you're tired
IE.work: Work with both a people-facing role and time to go deep alone. Listening to people, then taking it home and shaping it carefully (counseling, editing, research).
IE.key: After a day with people, take the same amount of time doing nothing. Connecting with people is your strength, but you only recharge alone.
IE.both: You have both the strength to think deeply on your own (I) and the strength to move with people (E). You can act naturally in front of others, yet you can only recharge in time alone.

worry: You want to see people, yet plans on the calendar start to feel heavy
After a stretch of time alone, your mood sinks for no clear reason
After a gathering you enjoyed, exhaustion suddenly hits
EI.work: Work with both time with people and time to focus alone suits you. Shaping ideas carefully and then delivering them to people, or working in a small team.
EI.key: Put both "people days" and "alone days" on your calendar in advance. When only one keeps going, the other strength starts to fade.
EI.both: You have both the strength to recharge through people (E) and the strength to think deeply on your own (I). Lively time and quiet time are both things you need. When either runs low, you tire easily.

worry: Plenty of ideas come to you, but none of them take shape
After talking big, you suddenly worry, "Can I really do this?"
The gap between ideal and reality often lets you down
SN.work: Work where you think up new things and then make them real with your own hands. Building products or services, planning improvements, crafting.
SN.key: Rewrite each idea as "one step I can take tomorrow." Using both imagining and checking turns ideas into reality.
SN.both: You have both the strength to check the facts in front of you (S) and the strength to imagine possibilities not yet visible (N). You can expand ideas, yet you can't settle until the ground under your feet is firm.

worry: You get everything done properly, yet something feels unfulfilled
Repeating the same method slowly gets boring
When asked what you really want to do, you can't answer well
NS.work: Steady work that still leaves room to invent new ways. Planning roles that know the front line, teaching, or being trusted with improvements.
NS.key: Once a week, make time to think "if I could do anything..." Adding imagination to your steady progress changes how your days feel.
NS.both: You have both the strength to imagine possibilities (N) and the strength to build on facts (S). You can move things forward realistically, yet without time to think "what's next?", days can feel flat.

worry: After agreeing to go along, you realize you actually disagreed
You have something to say, but swallow it for fear of spoiling the mood
You help others so much that your own matters get pushed back
TF.work: Work that asks you to support people and also make sound judgments. Counseling and support roles, HR, healthcare or education, team coordinator.
TF.key: Being kind and giving your opinion can go together. Try saying it in this order: "I understand how you feel. And here's what I think."
TF.both: You have both the strength to reason step by step (T) and the strength to sense people's feelings (F). You can stay gently by someone's side, yet inside you're calmly asking, "Is that really right?"

worry: You know the right answer, yet it takes you a long time to decide
After giving your opinion, you keep wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
Sometimes you lose track of what you really want to value
FT.work: Work where both logical thinking and understanding feelings come alive. Planning, marketing, editing, people-centered consulting.
FT.key: Hesitating is a sign you hold both strengths. Just write down "What does my heart say?" and "What does logic say?" separately, and what you're torn about becomes clear.
FT.both: You have both the strength to sense people's feelings (F) and the strength to reason step by step (T). You see what people with only one can't, but you also tend to get two answers inside: "my heart says this, logic says that."

worry: Even when you look fine, an undecided plan keeps nagging at you
After putting things off, you blame yourself
You're free to move as you like, yet somehow it wears you out
JP.work: Work where the big frame is set, but you can design how to get there. Project management, on-site coordination, event operations.
JP.key: You don't have to decide everything. Just pick three "things I'll do this week." Keep your flexibility, and simply having a view ahead will lighten you.
JP.both: You have both the strength to plan ahead (J) and the strength to flex in the moment (P). You can adapt to the unexpected, yet somewhere inside you can't settle without a view of what's ahead.

worry: Things are going to plan, yet somehow it isn't fun
Sudden changes irritate you, even when you understand why
"I have to do this properly" has become your catchphrase
PJ.work: Work with both moments to follow the plan and moments that need on-the-spot judgment. Sales, planning, front-line management, customer service.
PJ.key: Leave some time in your schedule with nothing planned, on purpose. Adding the joy of the moment to your planning makes it easier to keep going.
PJ.both: You have both the strength to flex in the moment (P) and the strength to plan ahead (J). You can organize things well, yet days packed with plans can start to feel suffocating.

worry: You're doing well, yet you still feel "it's not enough"
Worrying about what others think keeps you from bold steps
You dwell on small mistakes longer than you need to
AT.work: Work that needs both caution and decisiveness. Quality or risk management, healthcare, right hand to a leader.
AT.key: At the end of each day, write down three things you did today. Your care is a strength. Add a moment to remember the confidence you started with.
AT.both: You have both the strength to trust yourself and move forward (A) and the strength to check carefully (T). You act with care, yet sometimes you don't show the confidence you were born with.

worry: You look confident, so you can't share your worries with anyone
After deciding, you go over it again and again on your own
The more people rely on you, the harder it is to admit you're struggling
TA.work: Work with both a deciding role and a careful-checking role. Team leader, specialist, head of planning.
TA.key: Tell just one person you trust, "Honestly, I'm a little worried." Being careful isn't weakness. It's what makes your judgment solid.
TA.both: You have both the strength to check carefully (T) and the strength to trust yourself and move forward (A). You can decide without hesitating, yet inside you're quietly asking, "Is this really okay?"

same.both: Your temperament and character are the same type. You've grown the nature you were born with just as it is. Your sense of self is clear, and you don't waver easily.
worry: Places where your way doesn't fit cause you strong stress
The thinking of people unlike you can be hard to understand
The cause of your worries is often your surroundings or relationships, not you
same.key: When something doesn't fit, changing your place or your distance from people tends to work better than changing yourself.
same.work: If the way you work now feels right, that's your answer. When in doubt, trust your own sense.

letter.E: Gets energy from being with people
letter.F: Decides by what feels right for people
letter.J: Moves ahead with a clear plan
letter.AT_A: Moves ahead trusting their own judgment
letter.AT_T: Watches carefully and moves with caution
